newsitem.title: NORWAY: INTERNATIONAL GROUP FORMS SYNGAS PROJECT - STATOIL.
newsitem.headline: INTERNATIONAL GROUP FORMS SYNGAS PROJECT - STATOIL.

text.p: A consortium of five companies has launched an international project to develop and utilise ceramic membrane technology for converting natural gas into synthesis gas (syngas), Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday.
Syngas is the fundamental building block for producing synthetic oil, methanol and similar products.
Other partners in the five-year project are Amoco Production Co, British Petroleum Co Plc, Praxair of the United States, and South Africa's Sasol Technology.
Statoil said the high technology approach permits oxygen separation from air to be carried out alongside partial oxidation in a single unit.
"By making equipment lighter and more compact, energy and capital costs will be signifcantly reduced by comparison with existing syngas production methods," Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
The project group will hold its first meeting in Trondheim, Norway on August 18. Each partner will contribute technological expertise.
"The method can be used to produce syngas both on land and offshore," said Harald Torgaard, Statoil's representative on the steering committee.
"Applying it on our multi-purpose shuttle tankers represents a very interesting possibility."

Statoil said syngas production was particularly relevant for small gas fields and discoveries where gas and oil volumes were separately too small for commercial production, or at small fields which cannot be developed without a solution for utilising their gas.
